reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch attribute Bashemath's differing fathers to the ancient custom of renaming brides, with Moses preserving divergent genealogical sources unaltered.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Edom genealogy's variant arrangements as producing apparent contradictions, of which Bashemath's two fathers are an instance.

quotes.text: Nor are apparent contradictions wanting in the ethnographic genealogy. Ishmael, Edom, and the Cainite tribes first mentioned, come into mutual contact in different ways, which may be quite naturally explained from different views and arrangements of their mutual relationships.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Edom genealogy's internal variants.

sides.snippet: Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
sides.verseText: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.

sides.snippet: Basemath, Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
sides.verseText: and Basemath, Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
